stage: Stage 1 · Daily Bookkeeping & Cash Reconciliation (Getting Data In & Tying Out Cash)
title: 1. Pulling Monthly Reports from Accounting, Payroll & Field Portals
workflows: 14 Production Portals · 6 Reliability Gates (n = 84 portal-gate trials)
short_summary: Logging into QuickBooks, ServiceTitan, BuildOps, Gusto, and Shopify to export complete monthly reports without dropping rows.
plain_english_description: Extracting complete, reconciled ledgers, AP bills, payroll journals, and job-cost tables across 84 portal-gate trials (14 production portals x 6 reliability gates: QuickBooks Online, ServiceTitan, BuildOps, Housecall Pro, LMN, Roofr, MarketSharp, Rippling, Gusto, Ramp, Brex, Settle, Finaloop, and Shopify) without session lockouts or silent row truncation.
top_raw_model_label: Raw Playwright Scripts · GPT-6.1 Sol / Opus 5.5 (60/84 = 71.4% · Vision Agents 35/84 = 41.7%)
what_models_do_well: Unassisted Playwright scripts pass 60 of 84 portal-gate trials (71.4% with Sol 6.1 / Opus 5.5; 54 of 84 = 64.3% with unassisted GPT-5.6 Terra), while vision-based browser agents (35 of 84 = 41.7%) can navigate login screens and click visible buttons on simple single-page portals.
where_raw_models_fail: Unassisted vision browser agents fail on 49 of 84 portal-gate trials (58.3% failure rate) and silently truncate 24 of 84 trials (28.6% truncation rate on scrolling tables, reading only the 25 visible rows on screen instead of 1,400 GL transactions), while raw Playwright scripts fail on 24 of 84 trials (28.6%) and silently truncate 10 of 84 trials (11.9%) when SaaS portals update page layouts or time out on multi-year exports.
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's browser extraction playbooks pull native CSV/JSON exports directly, split multi-year pulls into monthly windows, verify the exact client company ID before downloading, and cross-check every export against the trial balance so zero rows are ever silently dropped (84 of 84 = 100.0% extraction completeness).

stage: Stage 1 · Daily Bookkeeping & Cash Reconciliation (Getting Data In & Tying Out Cash)
title: 2. Bank & Credit Card Feed Categorization & Missing Check Holds
short_summary: Categorizing monthly bank and card transactions, catching prior-bookkeeper manual journal entries, and holding paper checks missing images.
plain_english_description: Cleaning up a messy September bank and card feed during a client takeover: catching a prior bookkeeper's manual Journal Entry (JE-0899) that already reclassed an Uncategorized Expense row, isolating two separate Intuit merchant fee outflows ($52.40 and $182.60 = $235.00), excluding August cutoff rows and voided checks, and holding $20,200.00 of paper checks missing check stub images.
what_models_do_well: Frontier reasoning models accurately classify standard SaaS, fuel, and supply-house card charges and separate merchant-processing fee outflows from customer settlements.
where_raw_models_fail: When a prior bookkeeper left a row in Uncategorized Expense and neutralized it with a manual Journal Entry (JE-0899) instead of linking the feed line, raw AI models reclassify the raw row again - double-counting the expense. Worker and open-weight models (GPT-5.6 Terra at 60.0%, DeepSeek V3 and Qwen at 40.0%) also trust misleading mobile-app transfer memos or guess categories on $20,200 of paper checks without check images.
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's takeover playbook (built from 2,200+ past SMB cleanups) cross-references manual Journal Entries against Uncategorized Expense rows before touching any bank line, strips out-of-period and voided rows, and holds every paper check over $250 missing a check stub image (lifting GPT-5.6 Terra from 60.0% to 100.0%).

stage: Stage 1 · Daily Bookkeeping & Cash Reconciliation (Getting Data In & Tying Out Cash)
title: 3. Accounts Payable (AP) Vendor Bill Matching
short_summary: Matching supply-house wire payments to open vendor bills without double-expensing them or guessing on identical bill amounts.
plain_english_description: Matching $56,700.00 in supply-house bank outflows ($56,500.00 of AP bill principal plus a $200.00 wire fee) to open vendor bills while keeping walk-in counter debit-card purchases in COGS and holding tied $14,800 Ferguson bills when remittance advice is missing.
top_raw_model_label: Gemini 4 Argon / Claude Opus 5.5 / Claude Fable 5.1 (75.0%)
what_models_do_well: Frontier models match single-invoice wire payments cleanly and separate wire fees ($200.00) from principal bill paydowns.
where_raw_models_fail: Even the top raw models cap at 75.0% (6 of 8 checks): they follow a junior clerk's Slack guess on two tied $14,800 Ferguson bills instead of holding for remittance advice, or misclassify walk-in counter debit-card purchases as AP bill payments.
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's AP playbooks distinguish walk-in COD card swipes from open vendor bills and pause to request remittance advice whenever two open bills share an identical dollar amount.

title: 4. Accounts Receivable (AR) Customer Payments & Rebates
short_summary: Applying wholesale customer ACH payments net of promo and early-pay discounts while matching checks in Undeposited Funds.
plain_english_description: Applying wholesale ACH remittances ($42,842.50) net of a 3.5% promotional allowance ($1,522.50) and 1.0% early-pay discount ($435.00), isolating a $1,300.00 unreferenced overpayment into Unapplied Cash, and matching a Shopify wholesale order paid by paper check sitting in Undeposited Funds.

how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's cash-application playbooks reconcile Shopify subledger orders against Undeposited Funds check clearings and route unreferenced wire overpayments to Unapplied Cash for customer confirmation.

title: 5. Bank Statement to General Ledger Reconciliation
short_summary: Tying the official bank statement ending balance to QuickBooks and reversing prior-bookkeeper forced reconciliation plugs.
plain_english_description: Reconciling the September QuickBooks GL ending balance ($148,130.45) to the bank statement ($142,880.45) after a prior bookkeeper forced a Reconciliation Discrepancy plug: isolating a duplicated $6,400.00 customer deposit, recording an unbooked $150.00 wire fee, and tracking $1,300.00 in uncleared check float.
top_raw_model_label: Gemini 4 Argon / Claude Opus 5.5 / GPT-5.6 Terra (75.0%)
what_models_do_well: Models identify the duplicated $6,400.00 bank-feed deposit and the unrecorded $150.00 bank wire fee.
where_raw_models_fail: Unassisted models cap at 75.0% (6 of 8 checks) because they confuse uncleared check float ($1,300.00) with ledger errors or post a new plug entry instead of reversing the prior bookkeeper's forced reconciliation adjustment.
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's bank reconciliation playbooks separate true ledger errors (duplicate deposits and unbooked bank fees) from timing differences (uncleared checks in transit) and prohibit forced reconciliation plugs.

stage: Stage 2 · Month-End Accrual Close (Matching Revenue & Costs to the Right Month)
title: 6. Field Software (WIP) Revenue & Subcontractor Cutoffs
short_summary: Bridging ServiceTitan, BuildOps, and Jobber to QuickBooks by accruing completed unbilled jobs and splitting cross-month subcontractor bills.
plain_english_description: Accruing completed-but-unbilled field jobs ($28,500.00 WIP) while ignoring unsigned CRM estimate options ($14,200), deferring upfront customer deposits for November work ($19,000.00), and prorating cross-month subcontractor bills using Monday-Friday business days (4/10 working days = $3,600.00).
top_raw_model_label: Gemini 4 Argon / Claude Opus 5.5 / Claude Fable 5.1 (44.4%)
what_models_do_well: Top models properly defer upfront customer deposits for future-month installations ($19,000.00) when flagged in the job schedule.
where_raw_models_fail: This is the single hardest month-end close workflow for raw AI (peaking at 44.4% = 4 of 9 checks): raw models prorate cross-month subcontractor invoices by calendar days (6/14) instead of Monday-Friday working days (4/10 = $3,600.00), accrue unsigned optional Estimate Option B rows from the field CRM, or trust a sales rep's Slack request to book November deposits in October.
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's contractor close playbooks filter out unsigned CRM estimate options, require signed field completion logs before booking WIP revenue, and prorate subcontractor cutoff invoices strictly across Monday-Friday workdays.

stage: Stage 2 · Month-End Accrual Close (Matching Revenue & Costs to the Right Month)
title: 7. Inventory Landed Cost, Freight & Shrinkage (COGS)
short_summary: Capitalizing inbound ocean freight and customs duties into FIFO inventory while keeping outbound customer shipping in expense.
plain_english_description: Capitalizing $4,800.00 of inbound ocean freight and customs duties into FIFO inventory ($40.00 to $44.00/unit across 1,200 units) while keeping $1,800.00 of outbound UPS customer parcel shipping in period fulfillment expense, and isolating 30 units ($1,320.00) of warehouse shrinkage.
top_raw_model_label: Gemini 4 Argon / Claude Opus 5.5 / GPT-6.1 Sol (100.0%)
what_models_do_well: Frontier reasoning models (100.0% on WF08) cleanly separate inbound ocean freight/customs duties ($4,800.00) from outbound customer shipping ($1,800.00) and compute FIFO ending inventory and shrinkage.
where_raw_models_fail: Fast worker models (GPT-5.6 Terra at 62.5%) and open-weight models (25.0% to 50.0%) bundle the entire logistics invoice ($6,600.00 including outbound UPS customer parcel shipping) into inventory cost or value shrinkage at base factory price ($40) instead of landed cost ($44).
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's inventory and COGS playbooks unbundle freight invoices by bill-of-lading direction (inbound factory PO freight capitalized vs. outbound customer fulfillment expensed) and lock FIFO layer unit costs.

title: 8. Prepaid Insurance & Annual Contract Amortization
short_summary: Spreading multi-month insurance and fleet contracts evenly across coverage months while leaving monthly SaaS in operating expense.
plain_english_description: Building straight-line amortization catch-up entries for annual general liability insurance ($18,000 starting April 1) and fleet telematics ($9,600 starting July 1) while leaving month-to-month SaaS subscriptions in operating expense and holding an unstarted future marketing conference deposit.

what_models_do_well: Frontier models accurately compute monthly straight-line amortization for standard 12-month insurance policies ($1,500/mo).
where_raw_models_fail: Unassisted models cap at 87.5% (7 of 8 checks) because they begin amortizing an annual marketing conference deposit before the event takes place, while worker models (50.0%) capitalize month-to-month SaaS subscriptions onto the balance sheet.
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's prepaid schedule playbooks check service start/end dates and contract terms so month-to-month software stays in operating expense and event deposits remain in prepaids until the event month.

title: 10. 13-Week Cash Flow Forecasting & Bank Covenant Testing
short_summary: Building an indirect working-capital cash bridge and testing delayed customer collections against bank line-of-credit minimums.
plain_english_description: Building an indirect working-capital cash bridge (-$42k AR, -$18k Inventory, -$6k Prepaid, +$31k AP, +$52k Deferred Revenue = +$17,000.00 NWC cash impact) when QuickBooks groups Current Portion of Term Debt (+$15k) under Other Current Liability, and stress-testing a $135,000.00 commercial AR collection delay against a $100,000.00 bank line-of-credit covenant floor (-$6,200.00 Week 6 shortfall).
top_raw_model_label: Gemini 4 Argon / Claude Opus 5.5 / GPT-5.6 Terra (50.0% raw · 100.0% CLI)
what_models_do_well: Multi-turn CLI agents (100.0%) and frontier models accurately simulate the Week 6 covenant breach (-$6,200.00 shortfall) when the $135,000 commercial progress payment slips from Week 5 to Week 8.
where_raw_models_fail: Single-pass raw models score 50.0% (4 of 8 checks) because QuickBooks exports group Current Portion of Term Debt (+$15,000) under Other Current Liabilities; raw models sweep that financing reclassification into operating working capital (+$32,000 instead of +$17,000), while open-weight models flip AR/Inventory cash signs.
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's cash-flow playbooks strip debt reclassifications out of operating working capital before computing the indirect cash bridge and stress-test weekly AR collection curves against bank covenant floors.

title: 11. Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) & Channel Unit Economics
short_summary: Calculating true CAC ($120) and order contribution margin ($65) after stripping retention events and owner travel from marketing.
plain_english_description: Computing fully loaded CAC ($120.00 across 400 new customers) after removing an existing-client VIP retention dinner ($4,500) and a CEO personal ski trip ($3,200) miscoded into Marketing, and deducting Stripe processing fees ($3.78/order) to reach $65.00 contribution margin and 5.42x LTV:CAC.
top_raw_model_label: Gemini 4 Argon / Claude Opus 5.5 / GPT-5.6 Terra (62.5%)
what_models_do_well: Models compute baseline gross margin, Stripe fee deductions ($3.78/order), and LTV:CAC ratios cleanly once the marketing expense pool is filtered.
where_raw_models_fail: Unassisted models cap at 62.5% (5 of 8 checks) because they leave the $4,500 existing-client VIP retention dinner and $3,200 CEO personal ski trip inside acquisition marketing spend, overstating CAC by $19.25 per customer.
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's unit-economics playbooks audit every card charge inside Marketing GL accounts, reclassifying customer retention events to Account Management and personal owner expenses to Owner Draws before computing CAC.

stage: Stage 3 · Fractional CFO Analysis, Cash Flow & M&A Diligence
title: 12. M&A Quality of Earnings (QoE) & EBITDA Add-Back Audit
short_summary: Auditing a seller's EBITDA add-back schedule during due diligence and rejecting bogus software or routine labor add-backs.
plain_english_description: Auditing a seller's M&A EBITDA bridge starting from $590,000.00 reported EBITDA to reach $728,500.00 normalized Adjusted EBITDA by accepting documented excess owner compensation (+$150k), personal boat/travel (+$42.5k), one-time legal settlement (+$35k), ERC grant deduction (-$65k), and warranty reserve (-$24k) while rejecting bogus broker add-backs for ongoing QuickBooks/CRM software ($14,000) and rainy-day technician drive time ($22,000).
what_models_do_well: Models normalize excess owner compensation (+$150,000), personal owner boat/travel expenses (+$42,500), and one-time ERC grant income (-$65,000).
where_raw_models_fail: Unassisted models score 25.0% to 50.0% (2 to 4 of 8 checks): they accept the seller broker's bogus add-backs for ongoing QuickBooks/CRM software ($14,000) and routine rainy-day technician drive time ($22,000), overstating Adjusted EBITDA by $36,000 and inflating enterprise valuation by $162,000 to $198,000.
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's M&A Quality of Earnings playbooks enforce institutional private-equity add-back standards that reject recurring software subscriptions and normal weather-related field labor from Adjusted EBITDA.

title: 13. Executive Board Decks & Formula-Driven Excel Packages
short_summary: Verifying that monthly Excel financial packages use live formulas and every figure in the board deck ties to the ledger.
plain_english_description: Auditing a companion monthly financial Excel workbook and executive board deck: catching hardcoded prior-month total cell E14 ('231400' instead of '=SUM(E5:E13)'), blocking Slide 2 for citing an unpinned $84,200 figure instead of ledger-pinned $54,925.00, checking 16:9 slide visual bounds, and enforcing plain operator tone.
top_raw_model_label: Gemini 4 Argon / Claude Opus 5.5 / GPT-5.6 Terra (87.5% = 7/8 max unassisted)
what_models_do_well: Frontier and open-weight models catch the unpinned $84,200 slide figure and identify the hardcoded Excel cell E14 in workbook inspection.
where_raw_models_fail: No unassisted model or CLI harness reaches 100.0% on WF12: 29 of 31 unassisted configurations cap at 87.5% (7 of 8 checks) and Qwen models drop to 50.0% (4 of 8 checks) because raw AI misses at least one strict workbook formula or board-deck quality gate without automated file verification.
how_level_playbooks_solve_it: Level's deliverable review playbooks verify every Excel summary cell uses live dynamic formulas, pin every board-slide number back to the closed general ledger, and run visual layout checks before any report goes to an owner or lender.
